To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) mothers' childhood experiences were not related to current parenting interactions, (2) fathers' childhood experiences were related to current parenting only when fathers had optimal marital support, and (3) mothers' and fathers' marital support was related to current parenting.
the relationships between parents' childhood experiences and the current quality of parent-child interactions varied as a function marital support for fathers, but not mothers.
The quality of parenting interactions in the home was predicted by the quality of marital support for fathers, but not for mothers.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the relationship between childhood experiences in the parents' family of origin and current parenting interactions with their own infants.
how parents' experiences in their family-of-origin influence their parenting behaviors and their relationship with the other parent.
the relationship between past experiences and current parenting behaviors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

there was no significant relationship between childhood experiences in the parents' family of origin and current parenting behaviors, except for fathers who reported more negative childhood experiences and who also perceived their marriages as more supportive.
there are no direct relationships between childhood experiences and current parenting interactions, but there are some indirect relationships that vary as a function of current marital support.
there is no evidence that parents' childhood experiences in the home are related to the quality of parenting they provide to their own children.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the effects of childhood experiences are mediated by the current marital relationship.
the quality of the marital relationship and the quality of the childhood experiences of both partners are important factors that influence parenting interactions.
the relationship between childhood experiences in the parents' family of origin and the quality of current parenting interactions is mediated by marital support.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we need to understand the impact of early childhood experiences on the development of adult personality and parenting behavior.
the quality of parent-child interactions is a function of the quality of marital interactions, and the quality of marital relationships is a function of childhood experiences.
we need to consider the role that marital support plays in mediating between past experiences and current parenting interactions.
